lede: The hostile list is the single biggest entry on the budget — **6 to 8 of a 16-beacon minimum are a fight**, before anything else is rolled — and exactly one more beacon puts boarders on your ship, every run, no exceptions. Everything friendly is rationed to the same 1–2 the map gives anyone: one to two stores, one to two item beacons, and a neutral pool that is mostly other people's distress calls.
callout: **This is not a nebula sector, and it still allocates a nebula entry 0–5.** The same map generator can give you none of them or nearly a third of the sector inside the cloud, where the empty beacon's own text is "you can't see anything through the thick gases surrounding your ship". Ten of those 13 events arrive through the shared `NEBULA_REBEL` list, which is why several of them are drawn twice or three times over.

section_notes.HOSTILE_PIRATE: Four of the seven open with weapons already hot, and the three marked may-fight are not really escapes: {{PIRATE_ASTEROID}} offers one button, "Turn and fight"; {{PIRATE_NO_ESCAPE}} fights either way and the **Hacking** option only chooses whether your engines sit pinned at 1 for the whole fight or your Hacking system goes dark instead; {{PIRATE_SLAVER}} takes a crew member, or an **Engines 6** run that fails back into the fight one time in three.
section_notes.BOARDERS_PIRATE: Not a risk — a certainty. `min=1 max=1` means one of these five happens every run, with 2 to 5 humans on board. Only {{STATION_SICK}} and {{FLOATING_CARGO}} let you find out before you commit. This entry name is also defined elsewhere as a single event — 2–4 random-species boarders whose text is an unfinished placeholder string, which is a strong hint the list is the reading that ships.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_PIRATE: The deepest pool here, but only nine names in the file: one of them is the generic distress list, which is why 14 of these 22 events are somebody calling for help. {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} is the one named item in the whole sector — the **Damaged Stasis Pod**, and the file's own comment on that line reads "CRYSTAL UNLOCK". {{TRAP_BEACON}} is the reason to read the rest of them twice.
section_notes.NEBULA_PIRATE: `NEBULA_PIRATE` is also the name of a single event: a plain hostile pirate with five text variants and nothing else in it. If the engine resolves the name that way instead, this entire 13-event pool collapses into one repeated fight — which is a large difference for up to five beacons.
section_notes.DISTRESS_BEACON_PIRATE: Nine of these ten also sit in the neutral pool, so this entry mostly raises how often you get a distress beacon rather than what one can be. The exception is {{REFUGEE_DISTRESS_PIRATE}}, the pirate-sector swap for the generic refugee — refugees here trade fuel, missiles and drone parts instead of asking for charity.
section_notes.QUESTS_PIRATE: Allocated 0–1, so the sector can hand out no quest at all. Two events outside this entry plant a marker anyway: {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}} and {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} both point at the hidden Federation base.
section_notes.NOTHING_PIRATE: Even the empty beacon is pirate-flavoured: a ship de-cloaks behind you, you power up shields and weapons, and it flies past unimpressed.

steps.title: {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}}
steps.detail: The only multi-jump quest chain the sector's own quest entry can start — and that entry is allocated 0–1, so it may not be on the map. Saying yes rolls one of two jobs.

steps.title: Haul five drone parts
steps.detail: The parts arrive up front and a marker goes on the map. Half the time the station is there and lowballs you at 20–30 scrap — **Mind Control** or **Weapon Control 6** argues that back to 40–70, and the weapons version adds fuel. The other half, the station is silent, and what is behind the airlock is the same neurotoxin outbreak {{STATION_SICK}} runs.

steps.title: Or find the freighter that went missing
steps.detail: Three ways it lands: an intact wreck you can loot or deliver, a stranded crew who hand you the destination and a crew member, or the freighter still being chased by a pirate you have to shoot off it.

steps.title: Deliver, or keep the crates
steps.detail: Delivering pays out in drone parts at the destination. Keeping the cargo instead is a three-way roll: nothing you need, general military supplies, or a prototype weapon you install on the spot.

items.text: The most-used gate in the sector, and the only way into the boarding half of {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}} and {{NEBULA_LOST_SHIP}}.
Graded outs across the malfunctioning defense system, the plasma storm and the undetected Rebel — level 1 gambles, level 2 is clean, level 3 is better again.

Both events that hack **you** have a Hacking counter: the engine lockdown in {{PIRATE_NO_ESCAPE}}, and the sensor jam in {{BOARDERS_HACKING}} that otherwise leaves you at zero sensors with boarders already aboard.
Levels 2 and 3 both matter — {{STRANDED_BEACON}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}}, and the advanced-Medbay cure inside {{STATION_SICK}} that turns a boarding party into a recruit.
Scans the crates in {{FLOATING_CARGO}} before you bring them aboard — the same event that, unscanned, is a 2-in-4 chance of boarders.
Turns {{NEBULA_PIRATE_SMUGGLE}} into a bribe you can pocket, and buys a warning shot at {{PIRATE_CIVILIAN_BEACON}} that half the time scares the pirate off the civilian entirely.
**Damaged Stasis Pod** at {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} — the only named item in the entire pool.

34 events in this sector can put someone new on your ship. The slavers are the reliable ones: {{PIRATE_SLAVER}} and {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}} both offer a **Mantis, Rockman or Engi**, one by buying, one by killing.
A **human** from {{STRANDED_BEACON}}, and paid hires at {{TAVERN_HIRE}}.

1–2 guaranteed, plus two that are not on the budget at all: {{PIRATE_BRIBER}} can end with an arms dealer who normally only sells to Rebels, and {{MERCENARY_WORK_START}}'s dock rescue opens a shop and repairs 5 hull.
6 events plant a marker. Beyond the merchant chain, {{ESCORT_BEACON}} and {{QUEST_ESCORT}} both feed the same escort target, and two more point at the hidden Federation base.
41 of the 66 events are flagged unique, so the sector rewards jumping wide — repeats are far more likely to be the fights, which have no such flag.

9 events put people inside your hull and one of them is guaranteed. {{REFUGEE_GHOST}} is the worst-value version: five outcomes behind one "prepare to board", one of which is 2–4 humans and another of which just kills a crew member.
9 events can cost you someone. {{DISTRESS_INFESTATION}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} and {{STORM_ITEMS}} are the ones with no cheap way out if you arrive unequipped.
{{PIRATE_CHOICE}} charges 15–25 scrap to be allowed to leave, and {{PIRATE_SLAVER}} charges a crew member. Refusing either is a fight you did not choose the ground for.

{{TRAP_BEACON}} is a distress call that is a pirate, {{FLOATING_CARGO}} is free cargo that is boarders, and {{PIRATE_BRIBER}} pays you to watch someone else get robbed. The distress channel is not information in this sector.
{{MERCENARY}} sells 2 jumps of delay for 10–25 scrap, or a revealed map for 10–20. {{PIRATE_BRIBER}} can talk the Rebel scout you rescued into delaying the pursuit by 1.
{{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}} costs a jump to take, and both {{NEBULA_AUTO_WARNING}} and {{NEBULA_REBEL_UNDETECTED}} advance the fleet if the scout gets its message out.
Only two events in 66 move the clock in your favour, and both want scrap or a won fight first.
